sources.title: The Reconstruction and Stabilization of the Postwar Japanese Economy (Yale University Economic Growth Center)
sources.quote: The Korean War produced a sudden change in Japan's economic situation. As orders were concentrated in special procurement and munitions, exports grew rapidly along with the world wide demand accompanying military expansion. Markets boomed, inventory backlogs were wiped out, and mining and manufacturing production also started to increase at a fast tempo which eventually reached an increase of about 40% during the following one year. The balance of payments improved, sources of funds became plentiful, and profits rose as well.
